packages.name: yaml
packages.synopsis: Package yaml is a standard-library-only implementation of YAML 1.2: a parser, a schema resolver, a reflection-based codec and an emitter.
packages.doc:
Package yaml is a standard-library-only implementation of YAML 1.2: a
parser, a schema resolver, a reflection-based codec and an emitter.

# Overview

The Go standard library has no YAML support, so almost every project reaches
for a third-party module. This package fills that gap using nothing but the
standard library — no cgo, no generated parser, and a go.mod with zero
require directives. The API deliberately mirrors the shape people already
know from gopkg.in/yaml.v3 (Marshal, Unmarshal, Encoder, Decoder, Node), so
migrating is mostly a matter of changing the import path.

# Quick start

	var conf struct {
	        Name    string   `yaml:"name"`
	        Ports   []int    `yaml:"ports,flow"`
	        Verbose bool     `yaml:"verbose,omitempty"`
	}
	err := yaml.Unmarshal(data, &conf)
	out, err := yaml.Marshal(conf)

Streams of several documents are read with Decoder, which returns io.EOF
after the last document, and written with Encoder, which separates documents
with "---" and is flushed by Close.

# What the parser supports

Block sequences and mappings (including compact nesting such as "- key: v"),
flow collections ("[a, b]", "{k: v}"), explicit keys ("? key"), multi-document
streams ("---" and "..."), %YAML and %TAG directives, anchors and aliases,
merge keys ("<<"), plain, single-quoted and double-quoted scalars with the
full escape set (\n \t \" \\ \xNN \uNNNN \UNNNNNNNN), and literal ("|") and
folded (">") block scalars with strip, clip and keep chomping plus explicit
indentation indicators. Errors are *SyntaxError values carrying the line and
column at which the problem was found.

# Schema

Untagged scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema:

	null | ~ | (empty)        -> nil
	true | false              -> bool   (also True/TRUE/False/FALSE)
	0b1010 is NOT special; 12, 0o14, 0xC -> int
	1.5, 1e3, .inf, -.inf, .nan          -> float64
	everything else                      -> string

This is YAML 1.2, not YAML 1.1: "yes", "no", "on" and "off" are ordinary
strings, and sexagesimal numbers such as "12:30" are strings too. Explicit
tags (!!str, !!int, !!float, !!bool, !!null, !!seq, !!map, !!binary,
!!timestamp) override resolution, and unknown or local tags (!custom) are
preserved on the Node so callers can act on them.

# Nodes

Unmarshal into a *Node to get the document tree rather than Go values. A Node
keeps its kind, tag, anchor, presentation style, source position and its
head, line and foot comments, which is what makes comment-preserving
round-trips possible. Node.Decode converts a subtree into a Go value and
Node.Encode builds a subtree from one, so custom Marshaler and Unmarshaler
implementations can work at whatever level they prefer.

# Struct tags

Field names default to the lowercased Go field name. The `yaml` tag supports
a name plus the options "omitempty" (skip zero values), "flow" (emit this
field's collections in flow style), "inline" (hoist an embedded struct's
fields, or collect unmatched keys into a map), and "-" (ignore the field).
encoding.TextMarshaler and encoding.TextUnmarshaler are honoured for scalars,
time.Time uses RFC 3339, and time.Duration uses the time.ParseDuration
spelling.

# Errors

Decoding does not stop at the first field that does not fit: mismatches are
collected into a *TypeError while every other field is still stored. All
errors wrap sentinels, so they can be classified with errors.Is:

	errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrSyntax)
	errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrTypeMismatch)
	errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrUnknownAnchor)
	errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrAliasBomb)

# Alias-expansion guard

Aliases make it possible to write a small document that expands to an
enormous value — the "billion laughs" attack:

	a: &a [x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x, x]
	b: &b [*a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a, *a]
	c: &c [*b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b, *b]
	...

Decoding counts the nodes it visits, and a document that would expand past
the budget fails with an error wrapping ErrAliasBomb instead of exhausting
memory. Recursive anchors are caught by the same counter.

# Emitting

The emitter indents by four spaces by default (Encoder.SetIndent changes
that), quotes any scalar whose plain form would be read back as something
else, writes multi-line strings as literal block scalars when that
round-trips exactly, and falls back to double quotes when it does not. The
goal is stability — Unmarshal, Marshal, Unmarshal returns the same value —
rather than matching another implementation byte for byte.

This package is an independent re-implementation, MIT licensed, and is not
affiliated with or endorsed by the YAML project, PyYAML or js-yaml.

consts.doc:
Standard tags of the YAML 1.2 core schema, in the short "!!name" form used by
Node.Tag.

types.name: Decoder
types.doc: Decoder reads a stream of YAML documents from an io.Reader.

funcs.name: NewDecoder
funcs.doc:
NewDecoder returns a Decoder reading the YAML stream in r. The whole stream
is read on the first call to Decode.

methods.name: Decode
methods.doc:
Decode reads the next document from the stream and stores it in v. It returns
io.EOF once every document has been consumed.

types.name: Encoder
types.doc: Encoder writes a stream of YAML documents to an io.Writer.

funcs.name: NewEncoder
funcs.doc:
NewEncoder returns an Encoder writing to w. Documents after the first are
separated by a "---" marker. Close must be called to flush the stream.

methods.name: Close
methods.doc:
Close finishes the stream. It is safe to call more than once; subsequent
calls return nil.

methods.name: Encode
methods.doc: Encode writes v to the stream as one YAML document.

methods.name: SetIndent
methods.doc:
SetIndent sets the number of spaces added per nesting level. It panics if
spaces is not positive.

types.name: Kind
types.doc:
Kind identifies what a Node represents. Kinds are distinct bits so that they
can be tested with a mask, mirroring the layout used by gopkg.in/yaml.v3.

methods.name: String
methods.doc: String returns the kind's name, such as "mapping" or "scalar".

types.name: Marshaler
types.doc:
Marshaler is implemented by types that choose their own YAML representation.
The returned value is marshalled in place of the receiver; returning a *Node
gives complete control over tag, style and comments.

types.name: Node
types.doc:
Node is a single node of a YAML document tree. It preserves everything that
is needed to write a document back out unchanged in spirit: the node's kind,
its resolved or explicit tag, its scalar text, its anchor, its presentation
style, its source position, and the comments attached to it.

Unmarshal into a *Node (or a struct field of type Node) to obtain the tree
instead of Go values; Node.Decode then converts a subtree into a Go value on
demand, and Node.Encode builds a subtree from one.

funcs.name: Parse
funcs.doc:
Parse parses a YAML stream and returns one document Node per document. It is
the lowest-level entry point, useful for inspecting or rewriting a document
without converting it to Go values.

methods.name: Decode
methods.doc:
Decode decodes the node and its children into v, which must be a non-nil
pointer. It is the entry point used by Unmarshal for each document, and it
may also be called on any subtree obtained from a previously decoded Node.

methods.name: Encode
methods.doc:
Encode builds the node tree for v and stores it in n, replacing whatever the
node held before. It is the inverse of Node.Decode.

methods.name: IsZero
methods.doc:
IsZero reports whether the node holds no information at all, which is how an
omitted document or an absent value is represented.

methods.name: LongTag
methods.doc:
LongTag returns the node's tag in the fully expanded form, so "!!str" becomes
"tag:yaml.org,2002:str". Non-specific and local tags are returned unchanged.

methods.name: SetString
methods.doc:
SetString configures the node as a plain (or, when necessary, literal) string
scalar holding s.

methods.name: ShortTag
methods.doc:
ShortTag returns the node's tag in short form, resolving it from the value
through the YAML 1.2 core schema when the source carried no explicit tag.

types.name: Style
types.doc:
Style is a bit set recording how a node was written in the source, and how it
should be written back out by the emitter. The zero Style means "let the
emitter choose".

types.name: SyntaxError
types.doc:
SyntaxError reports a malformed YAML construct together with the position at
which it was detected. It wraps ErrSyntax.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc: Unwrap reports ErrSyntax so that errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrSyntax) succeeds.

types.name: TypeError
types.doc:
TypeError holds the accumulated per-value decoding failures of a single
Decode call. Decoding continues past a mismatched field, so a TypeError may
describe several unrelated problems at once; every other field is still
stored into the destination value.

methods.name: Unwrap
methods.doc:
Unwrap reports ErrTypeMismatch so that errors.Is(err, yaml.ErrTypeMismatch)
succeeds for any accumulated decode failure.

types.name: Unmarshaler
types.doc:
Unmarshaler is implemented by types that decode themselves from a YAML node.
The node is the fully parsed subtree assigned to the value, with its tag,
style and comments intact.

funcs.name: Marshal
funcs.doc:
Marshal encodes v as a YAML document.

Struct fields are named by their lowercased Go name unless a `yaml` tag says
otherwise; the tag supports "omitempty", "flow", "inline" and "-". Strings
that would be ambiguous as plain scalars are quoted, and multi-line strings
are written as literal block scalars where that round-trips exactly.

funcs.name: Unmarshal
funcs.doc:
Unmarshal decodes the first document of a YAML stream into v, which must be a
non-nil pointer.

Mappings decode into structs, maps or any; sequences into slices, arrays or
any; scalars are resolved with the YAML 1.2 core schema (null, bool, int,
float, otherwise string). Decoding a document into *Node yields the document
tree instead, preserving tags, styles, anchors and comments.

Fields that cannot be decoded do not abort the operation: they are collected
into a *TypeError which is returned once the rest of the document has been
stored.
